newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-David Jones looks at Rebel.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-David Jones looks at Rebel.

text.p: Sporting goods retailer Rebel Sports Ltd said on Wednesday it had held sale talks with retailers David Jones Ltd and Coles Myer Ltd, with each potential buyer signing a confidential agreement in return for a detailed information memorandum.

Stephen Higgs, a director at broker SBC Warburg, told Reuters that about six memorandums had been issued to local and overseas companies since Rebel chairman and founder Sam Linz revealed in November last year that he was a willing seller.
Higgs said there were ongoing talks with Coles Myer while he was not sure about David Jones' continuing interest since the abrupt departure of chief executive Chris Tideman on March 10.
Separately, Linz told Reuters that he regarded a Rebel share price of at least A$1.90 as a level which would attract him towards a sale of his 38 percent holding.
With 38.72 million shares on issue, Rebel would be valued at A$73.57 million with a share price of A$1.90.
Higgs said a full takeover of the company could achieve a price of more than A$2.00 per share.
Rebel shares were six cents higher at A$1.48 on Wednesday afternoon, with a 12 month high of A$1.90 and a low of 73 cents.
Higgs said the final sales price would be determined by how much of the Sydney-based sporting goods retailer was sold.
"It depends on whether the party is just going to buy 38 percent of a shareholder's interest or whether he is going to merge the whole group and get added value," he said.
"I mean you can see values over two bucks in that case. If you are just an investor in 20 percent or 38 percent then the value is probably nearer A$1.70."

Linz said he wanted to focus on the expansion of his privately-held Galore Group of barbecue retail outlets in the United States, where he said there could be up to 400 stores in the next few years compared with 35 at the moment.
He has allowed Rebel management and its advisers find a buyer and was not in any particular hurry.

"So what we have tried to do is to, with management, talk to groups who are demonstrating to us how they can add value to the group in terms of agency lines, (and and) extra rollout of stores either here or in Asia," Higgs said.
Rebel currently has 23 stores, mostly based in the state of New South Wales, with other operations in Queensland, Victoria and New Zealand.
The talks with companies such as David Jones was sometimes a slow process as the potential buyer reviewed its own strategy.

"We were clearly talking to groups like DJ's (David Jones) because you could roll out Rebel in all of the DJ stores," Higgs said. "But then you have now had a change of chief executive of DJ, they are going back through their whole business strategy with McKinsey's."
Rebel would have to wait to see if the new chief executive at David Jones, Peter Wilkinson, was keen to proceed.
Higgs said there was definite interest shown by Coles Myer, revealed by the Melbourne company's chief executive Dennis Eck in a weekend television interview.

The Myer Grace Bros unit of Coles is the main rival of David Jones, with analysts criticisting the latter company in recent months for losing its upmarket appeal. "There is ongoing dialogue (with Coles) at different levels," Higgs said. "But once again they have got their own strategy on sporting goods."
"He (Eck) said they are clearly watching it (Rebel) and I think it is probably up to us to go back to them. But at the moment we have got discussions going on with other parties."
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
